rv.q: But Young and Goldman (who I remember as part of the Chicago theater community) have penned a fine work that very deftly looks both at the legacy of one remarkable man and, in so doing, at the cause of the millions who died and left behind witnesses.
Writers Clark Young and Derek Goldman masterfully craft a lean narrative around this overwhelmingly complex and emotional story that packs a powerful punch in 90 minutes.
Delivered this way, Karski’s haunting lesson is unforgettable.
To this writer, the results are as transformative as the physical production.
Remember This: The Lesson of Jan Karski is a truly remarkable story of the power of a single person, and is a lesson for all of us about perseverance in the face of history and fate.
Strathairn's prodigious effort is something to remember.
Forceful, gripping, and indisputably exceptional, “Remember This: The Lesson of Jan Karski” is a superior piece of theatre.
Go see this impactful true story that will remind you that history remembers.

cn.t: David Strathairn delivers a mesmerizing, physically demanding tour de force as Polish Holocaust witness Jan Karski in this stark, compelling one-man show that poses urgent moral questions about duty and action.
